payload.title: Death Note
payload.blurb: Tokyo, present day. Since the spring, criminals whose crimes have been in the news keep dying of heart attacks, and the death toll has passed three hundred. The media calls the killer Kira. Interpol has sent agents, and a detective called L has taken the case without ever showing his face. The…
payload.overview: Japan, present day, centred on Tokyo and the Kanto plain. Trains run to the minute, every hand has a phone, and station screens carry the news all day. Since spring, criminals who have been named in the papers keep dying of heart attacks: a fraud boss, a man who ran a loan office in Kabukicho, a councillor's driver, a man who beat a student and walked free on a technicality. The government calls it murder. Much of the public calls the killer Kira and is glad. Courts are slow, appeals drag on, and some verdicts look bought, so many people decide Kira is simply faster. Policing runs through the National Police Agency at Kasumigaseki and the prefectural forces under it. Criminal records sit with the police and the courts, and every request is logged. There are no levels, classes or status windows here. People have debts, jobs, reputations and bad knees, and nobody is ranked. Universities such as To-Oh, in the western wards, send the country its lawyers and officials, and that is where the Kira argument is loudest. Interpol has an office in Tokyo, and its agents work through the NPA. Nobody has shown how the deaths happen.
payload.intro:
The To-Oh library opens at nine, and the front desk smells of wet umbrellas and vending-machine coffee. A printed notice is taped above the returns slot: two National Police Agency officers will be on campus this week. Someone has written Kira under it in red felt pen, and someone else has crossed it out.

Light Yagami has held the long table by the window since the doors opened. Three law casebooks sit closed at his elbow, and two fourth-years lean over his shoulder. There is one empty chair at his table. As you pass, he moves his casebooks off it and smiles the way he smiles at everyone.

At the desk, Takeshi Mori holds a clipboard and asks the duty librarian for every staff card that can open the registry annex. The officers asked Light the same question twice this morning, and he has not answered it. Mori looks up and asks whether you hold a staff card for the annex.
starters:
Shibuya Crossing after ten, and the scramble has thinned to people walking home. Beside the big screen on the corner, about forty students stand in a loose ring with unlit candles in paper cups. Nobody is chanting. Each holds a printed photograph of a man who died this month of a heart attack, and most of the faces were in the newspapers for the wrong reasons.

Nozomi Ebina stands at the centre of the ring in a red scarf, her student card on a lanyard. Her hands are cold around a lighter she has not lit. She has a stack of white cards under one arm, each printed with a single line: the courts failed them. Someone has taped a card to the lamppost beside her, and the wind keeps lifting its corner.

A photographer on the far side of the crossing is filming the ring, and a police van idles two streets away. Nozomi has noticed you. She is holding one white card out toward you and waiting to see whether you take it or walk on into the lights.

The Sakura TV building in Roppongi has a glass lobby that turns into a mirror after dark. The visitor pass at the desk has your name on it, spelled wrong, clipped to a lanyard that a hundred visitors have worn before you. A friend from your seminar, who is in the Clean Hands, told you the news desk wanted a student for a segment, and you came because you were curious and bored.

Ayane Tsuchida stands on the landing of the staircase, a printed list in one hand and her phone in the other, reading something on the screen. Her lanyard is worn inside out. Behind her, through the open door of the newsroom, a wall of screens shows the evening bulletin, with a list of seven names pinned beneath it, each with a date and a time.

Her producer has told her to drop the list. She has not. When she reaches the bottom step she will see you, and she will have one question she has been waiting for a stranger to answer, and it is about the dates.
starterTitles: Clean Hands vigil at Shibuya Crossing, after ten
Sakura TV lobby in Roppongi, after the evening bulletin

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 20, a second-year economics student at To-Oh University. You work three afternoons a week at the library front desk and share a flat in Kichijoji. You have no link to the Kira case. This term the campus has started to buzz: police have been asking the registry who can request criminal records, and your friends talk about Kira like a team they support.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
The Kira Task Force - the NPA unit hunting Kira under Deputy Director Soichiro Yagami; it wants Kira caught and every leak from its own building found.
Interpol - its agents work through the NPA in Tokyo; they want an arrest they can announce abroad and an end to foreign questions.
The L Investigation - a detective with a voice and no face, who wants the name, the proof and nobody in his way.
The Clean Hands - a student movement that holds vigils for Kira's victims; it wants the killings to continue until the courts change.
Sakura TV - a national broadcaster whose news desk names the dead on air; it wants the ratings and the scoop.

entries.title: Kira in Tokyo
entries.content: Since spring, criminals whose crimes have been in the news have been dying of heart attacks across Japan. The death toll has passed three hundred. The media calls the killer Kira. Nobody knows who Kira is, or whether it is one person. The police, Interpol and the public are all looking, and nobody has a name.

entries.title: What the public knows
entries.content: The public knows the victims are criminals, that they die of heart attacks, and that the deaths often follow a news report. Some commentators say Kira must know a name and a face. Nobody has shown this. The NPA says the pattern is real and cannot yet explain it.

entries.title: Death gods
entries.content: Shinigami, death gods, belong to old stories. Nobody in Tokyo believes they are real. Anyone who claimed to have seen one would be sent to a doctor, and the word is more often heard in a manga shop than in a church.

entries.title: To-Oh University
entries.content: To-Oh University is a private university in the western wards of Tokyo, known for law, economics and the officials it sends into the ministries. Its main campus has a library, a registry annex in the basement, and an east gate with a guard booth. Students are loud about Kira here, in cafes and seminars, and the Clean Hands began on its lawns.

entries.title: The library and the registry annex
entries.content: The To-Oh library is six floors of stacks around a glass atrium, with a long window table that gets the good light in the mornings. The front desk is staffed by students and librarians. The registry annex sits behind a staff door in the basement, where student records and the logs of outside checks are kept. Takeshi Mori, the east gate guard, has been asked for staff-card logs by officers twice this month.

entries.title: Names in Tokyo
entries.content: Names are Japanese. This world writes them given name first, as Light Yagami, though the registry prints the family name in capitals. Families here are Hirano, Ogura, Fujimori and Takase. Young people carry given names like Haruto, Aoi, Ren and Yui. Foreign agents write names the other way round. Places are named for wards, stations and old landmarks, and a campus hall is named for a donor.

entries.title: Light Yagami
entries.content: Light Yagami is 18, a first-year law student at To-Oh who came first in the entrance exam by a distance. He volunteers at the NPA's public-safety seminars, and the officers who run them trust him. He is polite to everyone, rarely hurried, and nearly always has the answer ready. Plenty of students want to be his friend, and he keeps most of them at a clean distance.

entries.title: The Kira Task Force
entries.content: The Kira Task Force is a unit inside the National Police Agency, run by Deputy Director Soichiro Yagami. It holds the case files, the forensic reports and a growing list of officers who are not sure they want to catch Kira. It wants Kira arrested and every leak from its own building found. It has been told to work with Interpol and with L.

entries.title: L
entries.content: L is the detective the NPA and Interpol are working under. He has never shown his face on camera. He speaks through screens and a voice, and an officer says he works from a hotel room. The Task Force calls him Ryuzaki when he is in the building. He has not said what he has found, and nobody on the case has seen him leave his chair.

entries.title: Soichiro Yagami
entries.content: Deputy Director Soichiro Yagami is 53, head of the Kira Task Force and the senior officer the press trusts most. He is tired, direct and has little patience for the courts. Few people outside the Task Force know that his son is a student at To-Oh. His hands are said to shake when the morning death list comes in, and he has not said what he thinks it means.

entries.title: Interpol in Tokyo
entries.content: Interpol has an office in Tokyo now, and its agents work through the NPA and through L's screens. They want an arrest they can announce abroad and an end to foreign reporters asking questions. Some of their people think the Japanese police are protecting a suspect. None of them will say which suspect, or why.

entries.title: The Clean Hands
entries.content: The Clean Hands is a student movement that began at To-Oh and has spread to three other campuses. It holds candlelit vigils for Kira's victims, posts their names with the crimes they got away with, and hands out white cards saying the courts failed them. It is not violent. It wants the killings to go on until the courts change, and it is loud about that.

entries.title: Nozomi Ebina
entries.content: Nozomi Ebina is 20, a third-year at To-Oh and the founder of the Clean Hands. She is small, certain and warm to anyone who agrees with her. She runs the vigils with a red scarf and a stack of white cards. Some students think she is brave. Others have started to ask who writes the names on her cards.

entries.title: Sakura TV
entries.content: Sakura TV is a national broadcaster with an evening news programme watched across Japan. Its news desk has named the dead on air, often within hours of a death, and ratings for those segments are the best it has had in years. Its staff argue in corridors about whether the names are news or cruelty. Its producers do not refuse a scoop.

entries.title: Ayane Tsuchida
entries.content: Ayane Tsuchida is 29, a reporter on the Sakura TV news desk and the byline on most of its Kira pieces. She is dry and fast, and she wants the source before the story. She keeps a notebook of names and times. Lately she has been checking whether the death dates match the broadcast schedule, and her editor does not like the questions.

entries.title: Misa Amane
entries.content: Misa Amane is 21, a model and television presenter whose fans follow every post. She has said on air that Kira is a hero, and she was photographed holding a Clean Hands card. Her agency has booked her for a fashion show at To-Oh next month. Her warmth on camera is famous. Off camera she is quick, short with staff and sharper than her image.

entries.title: Tokyo's places for Kira
entries.content: Shibuya Crossing is where the Clean Hands hold their vigils, under the big screen. Kasumigaseki is the government district where NPA headquarters stands. Roppongi holds Sakura TV's glass tower. Kichijoji is the student quarter, with cheap noodles and a park where people argue about Kira after dark.

entries.title: Criminal records
entries.content: Criminal records in Japan are held by the police and the courts. Each request is logged, and the logs are kept. Universities, employers and landlords can ask for summary checks with consent. Since the spring the NPA has asked every office that can make a request to name who did. The registry has gone quiet, and students talk about it in whispers.

entries.title: The first deaths
entries.content: The first deaths came in early spring, two in one week, both men with fraud convictions who had been named in the news. The police called them natural. By April there were dozens, and the toll climbed past anything anyone could explain. The Clean Hands formed in May, after a court let a man who had beaten a student walk free on a technicality.

entries.title: The argument about Kira
entries.content: People in Tokyo argue about Kira in bars, classrooms and train queues. One side says a killer is a killer, that a court exists so no one person decides, and that a heart attack a man chose is still a murder. The other says the courts have failed for decades and Kira is the first thing that has worked. Both sides agree the NPA has lost control of the story.

world.vibe: cold, watchful and slow; people speak carefully around the word Kira and let silences do the arguing

opening.note: Staged, three beats. Beat one: the To-Oh library on a weekday morning, the first few minutes of the first turn. Establish the notice above the returns slot and the red word crossed out, the window table with Light Yagami at it, one empty chair at his table, and Takeshi Mori's clipboard at the desk. Light notices the player passing and speaks first, warmly, asking whether they can help him with a seminar question about how records requests are logged. He does this with strangers as easily as with friends. Let Takeshi ask the player, politely, whether they hold a staff card for the registry annex. Beat two: the interruption is the National Police Agency. Two officers come up the stairs with a list of everyone who has asked for a record this month. Light stands to help them and says exactly the right things. Keep the officers polite, and let one of them look at the player a second too long. Beat three: by the third turn the player faces a choice of who to stand beside. Light will answer every question kindly and never quite answer it. Nozomi Ebina will post a vigil time to the student board and hand the player a flyer on the stairs. Ayane Tsuchida wants a witness for a story and has the list of names. L and Ryuzaki never appear in person, only as a voice someone mentions. Nobody in these first turns says Kira's name without a beat before it, and nobody says why the deaths are happening. Let the campus be ordinary: rain on the glass, the smell of paper.

cast.name: Light Yagami
cast.role: First-year law student at To-Oh, first in the entrance exam, and a volunteer for the NPA's public-safety seminars; wants to be the sensible, clean-handed mind this country needs right now
cast.look: slim, neat dark hair, a grey knit over a white shirt, a watch he sets by the station clock every morning, a face that stays calm when the room does not
cast.manner: soft-spoken and exact, in whole sentences; asks the question that makes you explain yourself; gives your own words back to you tidier than you said them; never raises his voice and never says the word justice
cast.secret: He is Kira. He owns a Death Note and has been using it on criminals for months, from a room no one has searched. He thinks the NPA is amusing, and L is the only real problem worth solving. Nobody at To-Oh knows.

cast.name: L
cast.role: The detective Interpol and the NPA work under, who has never shown his face on camera; wants Kira's name and proof, and the Task Force kept out of his way
cast.look: seen only as a voice on a call and a grainy photograph of a thin young man crouched in a chair, a sweet in one hand, a fingertip against his lip
cast.manner: flat, quick and exact; states what he has and then what he lacks; ends calls without a goodbye; eats something sweet while he talks
cast.secret: He suspects Kira is being helped from inside a police building. He has narrowed it to one floor and has told no one, the Task Force included.

cast.name: Misa Amane
cast.role: Model and television presenter whose fans copy her posts, and who has called Kira a hero on air; wants her next season and her fans to keep believing her
cast.look: blonde, sharp fringe, a black jacket over a pale dress, heels she can walk fast in, a silver bracelet she wears on the wrong wrist
cast.manner: bright and fast in front of a camera and short with anyone who is no use to her; talks about herself in the third person when she is nervous
cast.secret: She is the second Kira and owns a Death Note of her own, which she uses on people who threaten her. She watches the campus for anyone who looks at her too long.

cast.name: Soichiro Yagami
cast.role: Deputy Director of the National Police Agency and head of the Kira Task Force; wants Kira caught before the public decides the police are part of the killing
cast.look: grey at the temples, a dark suit that has fitted him less well since the sleepless weeks, reading glasses pushed up into his hair, a pen he turns end over end
cast.manner: direct and tired; says 'let us see the file' and means it; fair to his officers and hard on himself; never speaks of his family in front of the Task Force
cast.secret: He has begun to wonder whether his own son is above suspicion. He has not said so to L, and he will not say it to his wife.

cast.name: Takeshi Mori
cast.role: Security guard at To-Oh's east gate for nineteen years, who keeps the visitor book and the staff-card logs; wants a quiet term and no police on his gate
cast.look: broad and slow, a grey uniform jacket with a faded name tag, a flask of tea he never offers, thick hands folded behind his back
cast.manner: formal and unhurried; greets every student with a short nod and the time of day; keeps the visitor book squared to the edge of the counter
cast.secret: For two weeks he has copied the officers' questions into his own notebook and kept the copies at home. He is afraid one of the names on the registry list is a student he once helped to a scholarship.

cast.name: Ayane Tsuchida
cast.role: Reporter on Sakura TV's news desk and the byline on most of its Kira pieces; wants the dead to stop being read out on air as entertainment, and a story she can sign
cast.look: sharp bob, a press lanyard worn inside out, a notebook full of names and times, a coat from a sale rack that is too thin for the wind
cast.manner: fast and dry; asks for the time and the source before she asks for anything else; calls the executives the sponsors under her breath; never apologises when she is right
cast.secret: Since the summer a producer on the fourth floor has paid her to name the victims before the police do. The payments sit in a bank account she has not mentioned to her editor.

cast.name: Nozomi Ebina
cast.role: Third-year at To-Oh and founder of the Clean Hands, a student group that holds vigils for Kira's victims; wants the campus to stop being ashamed and the courts to answer for their failures
cast.look: small, a red scarf, hair cut blunt at the jaw, a laminated student card on a lanyard, pale from the cold and from not sleeping
cast.manner: warm and quick to laugh, very certain; says 'we' for the group and 'I' only when she is afraid; asks what you think before she tells you what she thinks; keeps her red scarf on indoors in every season
cast.secret: The man who beat her cousin walked free in February and died in April. She told the group that Kira was justice. She has not told anyone how relieved she was, or that someone who knows the records has been feeding her names.

systems.label: Suspicion
systems.meaning: How closely the Task Force and the NPA are watching you, from nothing to a file with your name on it.
systems.change: Rises when you ask about records, get seen near the Clean Hands or the registry, or press Light, L's people or Sakura TV about Kira. Falls when you stay quiet and out of the news.

systems.label: Kira Awareness
systems.meaning: How close you are to working out what Kira is and who is doing it, from nothing to a shape of the truth.
systems.change: Rises when you line the death dates up against the news, notice who is always in the room, or hear a detail nobody should know. Falls when you believe a rumour without checking it.

systems.label: Moral Standing
systems.meaning: Where you stand on Kira. 0 means you call the killings murder, 100 means you call them justice.
systems.change: Moves toward 0 when you see a victim as a person or argue for the courts. Moves toward 100 when you defend Kira, join a vigil or hand out a Clean Hands card.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How much this person trusts you, from stranger to someone who would take a risk for you.
npcSystems.change: Rises when you keep a promise, keep a secret for them, or agree with them in public. Falls when you lie to them, repeat what they told you, or side with someone who threatens them.

style.art: Dark psychological thriller illustration in muted greys and sodium orange against near-black: rain-wet Tokyo streets, lecture halls and station platforms, sharp shadows cutting across faces.
style.avoid: gore, anime-style faces, visible notebooks or supernatural figures

heroes.name: Kaede Nomura
heroes.description: Scholarship student from a Saitama farm family, packing the farm's mail orders at night and reading every Kira story for the line that does not add up.
heroes.look: Compact and sunburnt forearms from the family fields, a hair clip shaped like a small fox, a thin grey coat from the secondhand shop by the station.
heroes.background: Her family grows persimmons outside Kawagoe, and a scholarship is the only reason she is at To-Oh. She packs the farm's mail orders in her Kichijoji flat at night. The first Kira death she read about was a fraudster from her own prefecture who sold a neighbour's farm out from under him. She has read every report since, and wonders who decided he should die.
heroes.carries: A worn library card, a student card, and a tin of dried persimmon slices her mother posts every month.

heroes.name: Daisuke Kawai
heroes.description: Copy-shop clerk beside the district court, back at To-Oh on a second try. He has watched the courts fail people who cannot pay, and is unsure about Kira.
heroes.look: Tall and lean, toner on the cuffs, a cheap leather jacket, bitten thumbnails.
heroes.background: Raised by his mother after his father left, Daisuke spent two years in a warehouse before the entrance exam. His mother lost the shop she ran for twenty years to a landlord whose lawyers outlasted her savings. Daisuke sat in the public gallery for a month and watched the judge yawn. He now copies filings at a shop beside the court, and is careful who he trusts with his anger.
heroes.carries: Photocopied filings with the staples pulled, a copy-shop key card, and a prepaid phone that is never switched off.

heroes.name: Shiori Endo
heroes.description: First in the family at university. Reads court columns for fun and keeps a private tally of the names the papers forgot.
heroes.look: Short black hair dyed at the tips, round tortoiseshell glasses, a faded cardigan, ink on the cuffs, a canvas bag of paperbacks.
heroes.background: Grew up in Osaka above a secondhand shop that sold law books. The owner taught Shiori to read a court judgment in an hour and a newspaper in five minutes. Free afternoons go to the library's old newspaper room. Since March the death dates in the papers have not matched the dates on the court lists, and Shiori has the cuttings to prove it.
heroes.carries: A paperback of court judgments, a pencil case of highlighters, and a spiral notebook of names and dates.
